results.title: Best App Blockers for Android in 2026 (Free and Paid)
results.content:
AppBlock by MobileSoft blocks apps and websites on Android and iPhone, with browser extensions for Chrome, Edge and Brave. Its Strict Mode locks your settings until a timer or schedule ends, until you enter a PIN, or until the phone is on the charger, and it can add a cooldown or require a partner's approval before you can change anything. It can also prevent uninstalling through Android's device admin.

 Price: free on Android for up to 3 apps, 3 websites and 3 schedules, with Strict Mode up to 24 hours. The paid plan on iPhone in the US is $4.99/month or $29.99/year; Android prices are shown in the app.
 Pros: very hard to bypass in Strict Mode; 10M+ downloads on Google Play.
 Cons: designed for self-control, not for managing someone else's phone remotely. [...] ### 6. FamiSafe: app rules plus location

Best for: parents who want app blocking together with location alerts.

FamiSafe by Wondershare works on Android, iPhone, Windows, Mac, Kindle Fire and Chromebook (via extension). It offers app rules and limits, a web filter, live location, geofences, YouTube controls and keyword alerts in social apps. On Android, removing it requires a password; on iPhone there's no uninstall protection.

 Price: $9.99/month, $19.99/quarter or $59.99/year. The free tier covers 1 device with most features locked.
 Pros: broad feature set; uninstall password on Android.
 Cons: the free tier is too limited to judge it; weaker protection on iPhone.

01

### Free core, no ads

The core app is fully usable without Premium, ads or a physical tag. Premium and tags support development instead of acting as a mandatory subscription or ad-removal fee.

02

### Open source

The public source repository makes the project easier to inspect, follow and trust than a completely closed blocker app.

03

### Flexible friction

Use profiles, schedules, Quick Actions, NFC, QR, barcode, website blocking and supported in-app blocking depending on how strict you want the setup to feel.

results.title: 8 Phone Blocking Apps You Should Try Instead Of Brick
results.content:
If you want dedicated hardware for blocking apps, but don't want to spend $60, Bloom is a good alternative. Unlike the Brick, it comes in the form of a metal card that's discreet and easy to store. The concept is similar to Brick. You tap the Bloom card on your smartphone to lock the device, and then tap it again to unlock the restrictions. Once it's locked, hide the card, give it to your spouse, or leave it in a different room.

The Bloom card and the Bloom app work on both iPhone and Android, and the app itself is free, with no subscriptions or in-app purchases. The card costs $39. While deleting the Bloom app from your smartphone can unblock apps, Bloom offers a strict mode that stops you from deleting any app from your smartphone until the time is up, or it's unlocked using the card. [...] ScreenZen popup for opening a blocked app.  ScreenZen

If you're on the hunt for a truly free screen-time utility that works across major platforms like iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, and iPad, take a look at ScreenZen. There are no premium tiers here, though you can donate to show your support for the developer. ScreenZen is not technically an app-blocking utility, but it will annoy you into submission.
